A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PI-DEF research work, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–D. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation results for emissivity and velocity reconstruction, baseline comparisons in Table 1, and sensitivity and ablation results, including Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results, including Table 1 and the appendix velocity-mismatch ablation.

M1.justification: The emissivity and velocity networks, rendering procedure, three loss terms, and optimization procedure remain unchanged. Renaming indices in Eqs. (9) and (14) does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same simulated emissivity fields and full-image, EHT 2017, EHT 2025, and ngEHT measurement scenarios. Noise conditions and spin-sensitivity coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: BH-NeRF and the physics-agnostic 4D-MLP remain the comparison methods in Table 1 and Figure 3. Comparator membership in the other reported comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The five-field evaluation, metrics, measurement simulation settings, network configurations, and optimization budgets are unchanged. The iteration symbol changes from i to s in Eq. (14), but its decay schedule and parameter values remain identical.

E4.justification: The measurement-sparsity, emissivity-signal, velocity-parameterization, noise, and spin-sensitivity analyses are retained unchanged. Appendix A and Figure 10 contain the same velocity-prior mismatch ablation.

E5.justification: Table 1 reports the same mean and standard deviation across five test emissivity fields in both versions. No seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains PSNR means of 37.3, 35.4, and 34.0 dB and MSE means of 2.3, 3.8, and 4.9 × 10^-5 for PI-DEF, 4D-MLP, and BH-NeRF, respectively, with identical standard deviations. Numerical and qualitative results throughout Figures 3–10 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 corrects the final phase factor in Eq. (17) from exp(i(φ_k−φ_j)) to exp(i(φ_k−φ_i)), making it consistent with the cancellation in Eqs. (18)–(19). Appendix D.2 changes the bound following Eq. (31) from γ² > 1 to γ² ≥ 1, although the separate preceding γ > 1 physicality statement remains.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint emissivity and velocity recovery, improved simulated reconstruction over the baselines, and potential inference of black-hole spin.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning weak emissivity, near-horizon velocity recovery, noise, and spin inference remain unchanged. Section 3.1.3 clarifies the wording about neglecting finite light-travel time without introducing a different approximation or limitation.

D1.justification: Sections 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same architecture, hyperparameters, simulation instructions, solver, hardware, and runtime information. The removed generic Overleaf URL was stray text rather than a code or data access instruction.

R1.justification: The introduction corrects the attribution of the first 3D flare recovery from Levis et al. (2022, reference 27) to Levis et al. (2024, reference 28). Both works were already cited; the bibliography and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar, spelling, punctuation, and notation corrections, clarifies the light-travel-time explanation, and removes an accidentally appended Overleaf URL. Section order and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Limited text reflow on pages 5–6 moves existing optimization-setting lines across the page break and changes paragraph spacing. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–2 retain their displays, captions, structures, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 improves local mathematical consistency through the closure-phase correction and revised bound, corrects a scientific attribution, and improves readability through wording and typo fixes. These are useful but limited gains; the method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
